structure.note: One class of common stock. Schwab formerly also had nonvoting common stock, all held by TD Bank; on February 12, 2025 TD sold its stake and the company repurchased TD's remaining 19.2 million nonvoting shares, which converted into common stock, so only voting common stock has been outstanding since. Charles R. Schwab, the founder and co-chairman, holds 5.9%; the 2026 proxy's table lists BlackRock (5.6%) as the only other holder above 5%.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Documents read on sec.gov: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0000316709-26-000009) and 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-26-142826). OWNERSHIP: 'Percent of Outstanding Shares' as of March 3, 2026; only one class of common stock is outstanding. Charles R. Schwab, co-chairman (the proxy letter is signed by him and Walter W. Bettinger II as Co-Chairman), beneficially owns 103,039,913 shares (5.9%), including 844,613 he can acquire within 60 days, shares held by trusts for which he or his spouse is trustee, 30,483,368 held by family limited partnerships, and 6,411,826 held by nonprofit public benefit corporations he established, for which he disclaims beneficial ownership. Family members' separate holdings, such as director Carolyn Schwab-Pomerantz's 1,706,738 shares, are not added. HOLDERS: the 2026 table lists only BlackRock among other 5% holders, based on a Schedule 13G/A filed January 31, 2024 (the asOf is that filing date, so it is stale). Vanguard, listed in the 2025 proxy, is not in the 2026 table; the proxy's related-person section says BlackRock and Vanguard each owned more than 5% at some point since the beginning of 2025. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow 'Dividends paid' line ($2,329 million) combines common and preferred. The 10-K's dividend table reports cash paid on common and nonvoting common separately ($1,958 million, $1.08 per share), so that figure is used; preferred dividends are excluded. BUYBACKS: $7,346 million of common and nonvoting common repurchases, including the $1.5 billion repurchase of TD's remaining 19.2 million nonvoting shares on February 12, 2025 and 58.2 million common shares for $5.5 billion under the new $20 billion authorization; the $2,458 million redemption and repurchase of preferred stock is excluded. GEOGRAPHY: null. Schwab reports two segments (Investor Services and Advisor Services) and the 10-K gives no revenue-by-geography table.

ecosystem.notes: Client assets are a stock (the market value at period end of all client assets in Schwab's custody, BDA balances and proprietary products, cash and securities). No take rate is computed on them. The 10-K also reports net new client assets of $498.6 billion in 2025 (core: $519.4 billion); that is net client money moved onto the platform, not volume transacted through it, so it is not used as a measure. Total net revenues include net interest revenue ($11.75 billion in 2025).

taxes.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Taxes: income taxes paid, net of refunds received (us-gaap:IncomeTaxesPaidNet), from the income-tax note's table by jurisdiction (federal 1,089, state 480, foreign 6; California 216). R&D not reported as a separate line (broker/bank).

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0000316709-26-000009). Broker with a bank (Charles Schwab Bank): operating cash flow is driven by client receivables and payables and segregated investments, not by revenue collection, so paidOut is null and altPaidOut = noninterest expense − D&A − SBC + income taxes paid (PAIDOUT.md). D&A is both income-statement lines inside total expenses excluding interest: depreciation and amortization (850) and amortization of acquired intangible assets (512). Interest paid (4,557) is shown separately. Capex (548) is recorded for reference and is not in altPaidOut. Revenue is net of interest expense (3,754). Income taxes paid are net of refunds, from the income-tax note.
